content.title: About
content.content: Plain carbonated water is pure drinking water infused with carbon dioxide. It contains no sugars, flavors, or colorants and is suitable for hydration and culinary use.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial method of carbonating water was developed in the early 19th century.
Carbonation can enhance the perception of taste, which is why it is often used in cocktails and soft drinks.
In some countries, carbonated water is served instead of still water as a restaurant tradition.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Like still water, carbonated water helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Moderate consumption may promote a feeling of fullness and aid digestion in some individuals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Higher acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Tooth enamel erosion
items.content: Frequent intake may contribute to enamel demineralization, especially if not followed by rinsing with plain water.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink chilled, use as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails, mixers, and in cooking (e.g., for batters).

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container protected from light. After opening, consume within a few days.
